source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Economic Development, Ch. 7 (Environment and Sustainable Development).

sections.heading: 1. Environment and Its Functions
points: The **environment** = the total of all surroundings (biotic + abiotic) that support life.
Problems arise when the demand on the environment exceeds its **carrying capacity**.

sections.heading: 2. Environmental Crisis
points: Rising population, affluence and technology have led to **over-exploitation of resources and excess waste**.
Problems: **air/water/land pollution, deforestation, ozone depletion, global warming, loss of biodiversity, falling water table**.
In India: **land degradation, water pollution, air pollution (among the world's most polluted cities)**, and shrinking forests.

sections.heading: 3. Sustainable Development
points: **Sustainable development** = development that meets the needs of the present **without compromising the ability of future generations** to meet their own needs (Brundtland Commission).
It balances **economic growth, social equity and environmental protection**.
The **Rio Earth Summit (1992)** and **Agenda 21** promoted it globally.

sections.heading: 4. Strategies for Sustainable Development
points: Use of **non-conventional/renewable energy** (solar, wind); **LPG and CNG** for cleaner fuel; **biogas** in rural areas.
**Wind and solar power**, mini-hydel plants; **traditional knowledge** and practices.
**Recycling, afforestation, water harvesting**, and controlling pollution.
The goal is intergenerational equity and ecological balance.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Environment functions: supplies resources, assimilates waste, sustains life, aesthetics.
Problems arise when demand exceeds the environment's carrying capacity.
Sustainable development (Brundtland): meet present needs without harming future generations.
Rio Earth Summit (1992) → Agenda 21.
Strategies: renewable energy (solar/wind), CNG/LPG, biogas, recycling, afforestation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Sustainable development** = meeting present needs **without harming future generations** (Brundtland).
Environmental crisis arises when demand **exceeds carrying capacity**.
**Agenda 21** came from the **Rio Earth Summit (1992)**.
Strategies stress **renewable/non-conventional energy** (solar, wind, biogas).
